post.youtube_title: Jewelry render basics: how diamond color is graded
post.caption: Diamond color is graded D to Z, from colorless to light yellow or brown. That makes 23 letter grades in five groups: colorless runs D to F, and near colorless runs G to J. Graders judge loose stones, face down, against master stones, on a scale GIA built in the early 1950s. The gap between neighboring grades is slight and often hard to see, and many guides say G to J can look white in a setting. Yellow gold can soften a tint, and white metal can show it, while fancy colors like pink and blue use a separate scale. A render shows a client the metal around the stone before the piece is made. The renders in this video were made with HeyGema.
